official_sources.source_title: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) Exam Guide

sources.source_title: AIF-C01 Content Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML

topics.name: Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
subtopics: AI, ML, deep learning, GenAI, and agentic AI
models, algorithms, training, inference, bias, fairness, and fit
batch, real-time, asynchronous, and serverless inference
labeled, unlabeled, structured, unstructured, tabular, time-series, image, and text data
supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning

content.scope_summary: Candidates distinguish AI, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, and agentic AI, and understand how models, algorithms, training, inference, bias, fairness, and fit relate. The scope includes common inference modes, data forms, and supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
content.question_focus: Definitions, comparisons, and selection of the correct term for a described learning, data, or inference scenario.

topics.name: Identify practical use cases for AI
subtopics: AI value, scalability, automation, and decision support
cost-benefit and cases where prediction is inappropriate
regression, classification, and clustering
computer vision, NLP, speech, recommendations, fraud detection, and forecasting
AWS managed AI services
traditional ML compared with foundation models

content.scope_summary: Candidates recognize business situations where AI adds value and situations where cost, constraints, or the need for a guaranteed outcome make AI unsuitable. They map regression, classification, clustering, foundation models, and managed AWS AI services to appropriate use cases while considering regulation, explainability, and operations.
content.question_focus: Business-scenario technique selection and identification of suitable managed AWS capabilities.

topics.name: Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
subtopics: AI/ML pipeline stages and components
open pre-trained and custom model sources
managed and self-hosted production APIs
AWS services across the lifecycle
MLOps, monitoring, retraining, repeatability, and production readiness
model and business evaluation metrics

content.scope_summary: The lifecycle covers pipeline components, model sourcing, production access patterns, and matching AWS services to lifecycle stages. MLOps emphasizes experimentation, repeatable and scalable processes, monitoring, retraining, technical-debt management, and production readiness. Evaluation combines model metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 with business outcomes such as cost, feedback, and ROI.
content.question_focus: Lifecycle ordering, service-stage matching, MLOps responsibilities, and choosing an evaluation metric.

sources.source_title: AIF-C01 Content Domain 2: Fundamentals of GenAI

topics.name: Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
subtopics: tokens, chunks, embeddings, vectors, prompts, transformers, LLMs, and foundation models
multimodal and diffusion models
GenAI application use cases
foundation-model lifecycle
token pricing and context engineering
agentic AI, MCP, memory, tools, communication, and orchestration

content.scope_summary: The scope connects tokens, chunking, embeddings, vectors, prompts, transformer-based LLMs, foundation models, multimodal models, and diffusion models. Candidates understand common GenAI uses, the foundation-model lifecycle, token-based inference cost, and context engineering. Agentic concepts include tools, memory, orchestration, multi-agent communication, and MCP connections to external systems.
content.question_focus: Concept identification, lifecycle stages, cost effects, and agent-component responsibilities.

topics.name: Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
subtopics: adaptability, responsiveness, conversation, and content generation
hallucination, interpretability, inaccuracy, and nondeterminism
model capability, constraints, compliance, cost, latency, and complexity
business value and outcome metrics

content.scope_summary: GenAI can provide adaptable, responsive, conversational content generation, but it can also hallucinate, behave nondeterministically, be inaccurate, and be difficult to interpret. Model selection balances capabilities and performance against constraints, compliance, cost, latency, and complexity. Business evaluation uses outcomes such as ROI, efficiency, conversion, accuracy, and customer value.
content.question_focus: Tradeoff analysis, model-selection constraints, and selecting a business metric.

topics.name: Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
subtopics: Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker AI, SageMaker JumpStart, Amazon Quick, Kiro, Strands Agents, and Bedrock AgentCore
accessibility, efficiency, cost effectiveness, and speed to market
security, compliance, responsibility, and safety
availability, redundancy, performance, regions, tokens, throughput, and custom-model tradeoffs

content.scope_summary: Candidates identify AWS services used to develop GenAI applications and explain how managed capabilities can lower barriers, improve efficiency, accelerate delivery, and support business outcomes. AWS infrastructure considerations include security, compliance, responsibility, and safety. Cost tradeoffs involve responsiveness, availability, redundancy, performance, regional coverage, tokens, provisioned throughput, and custom models.
content.question_focus: AWS service identification and architecture or cost tradeoff selection.

sources.source_title: AIF-C01 Content Domain 3: Applications of Foundation Models

topics.name: Describe design considerations for applications that use foundation models
subtopics: foundation-model selection criteria and inference parameters
RAG and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
AWS vector database options
customization cost tradeoffs
AI agents and business applications

content.scope_summary: Foundation-model selection considers cost, modality, latency, languages, size, complexity, customization, context length, output length, and prompt caching. Temperature and length settings affect responses. RAG grounds applications with retrieved knowledge; AWS vector options include OpenSearch Service, Aurora, Neptune, and RDS for PostgreSQL. Customization choices include pre-training, fine-tuning, in-context learning, RAG, and distillation.
content.question_focus: Architecture choice, RAG/vector storage, inference settings, and customization tradeoffs.

topics.name: Choose effective prompt engineering techniques
subtopics: context, instructions, and negative prompts
zero-shot, single-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and templates
specificity, concision, experimentation, guardrails, and response quality
prompt exposure, poisoning, hijacking, and jailbreaking
Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management

content.scope_summary: Prompt engineering combines context, instructions, and constraints. Techniques include zero-shot, single-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, and reusable templates. Effective prompts are specific, concise, tested, versioned, and protected with suitable guardrails. Risks include prompt exposure, poisoning, hijacking, and jailbreaking; Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management supports prompt versioning and management.
content.question_focus: Selecting a prompting technique, improving a prompt, managing versions, or identifying a prompt risk.

topics.name: Describe the training and fine-tuning process for foundation models
subtopics: pre-training, fine-tuning, continuous pre-training, and distillation
instruction tuning, domain adaptation, and transfer learning
data curation, governance, size, labeling, representativeness, and RLHF

content.scope_summary: Foundation-model development can use pre-training, fine-tuning, continuous pre-training, and distillation. Fine-tuning approaches include instruction tuning, domain adaptation, transfer learning, and continued training. Preparation requires governed, curated, sufficiently sized, labeled, and representative data; human feedback can be incorporated through RLHF.
content.question_focus: Choosing a training method and identifying data-preparation requirements.

topics.name: Describe methods to evaluate foundation-model performance
subtopics: human evaluation, benchmark data, and Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, and LLM-as-a-judge
business objectives and application evaluation
task completion, satisfaction, and cost per interaction

content.scope_summary: Foundation models can be evaluated with humans, benchmark datasets, and Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation. Relevant measures include ROUGE, BLEU, BERTScore, and LLM-as-a-judge. Application evaluation also covers RAG, agents, and workflows, and must connect technical results to task completion, user satisfaction, productivity, engagement, and cost per interaction.
content.question_focus: Selecting an evaluation approach or metric for a technical or business objective.

sources.source_title: AIF-C01 Content Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI

topics.name: Explain the development of responsible AI systems
subtopics: bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, and veracity
Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sustainability and model selection
legal and customer risks
inclusive, diverse, curated, and balanced datasets
bias monitoring, subgroup analysis, human audits, and Amazon A2I

content.scope_summary: Responsible AI considers bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, truthfulness, sustainability, and legal or customer risks. Dataset quality depends on diversity, balance, inclusion, and curation. Bias and variance can cause demographic harm, inaccuracy, overfitting, or underfitting. Guardrails, label analysis, subgroup analysis, human audits, and Amazon A2I help detect or monitor problems.
content.question_focus: Recognizing a responsible-AI risk, dataset issue, monitoring method, or guardrail use.

topics.name: Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
subtopics: transparent, explainable, and opaque models
SageMaker Model Cards and Bedrock Model Evaluations
open models, data, and licensing
safety, interpretability, and performance tradeoffs
human-centered design and user feedback

content.scope_summary: Candidates distinguish transparent or explainable models from opaque ones and understand the tradeoff between interpretability, safety, and performance. SageMaker Model Cards, Bedrock Model Evaluations, open model information, data documentation, and licensing can support transparency. Human-centered design includes user feedback and clarity about AI-assisted decisions.
content.question_focus: Choosing a transparency tool or identifying an explainability and performance tradeoff.

domains.name: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

sources.source_title: AIF-C01 Content Domain 5: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

topics.name: Explain methods to secure AI systems
subtopics: IAM, encryption, Macie, PrivateLink, shared responsibility, AgentCore identity and policy, and Bedrock Guardrails
source citation, lineage, catalogs, and SageMaker Model Cards
data quality, privacy, access control, and integrity
prompt injection, leakage, filtering, validation, logging, and toxicity
RAG grounding, output validation, and confidence scoring

content.scope_summary: AI security combines identity and access control, encryption, private connectivity, data discovery, shared responsibility, guardrails, and AgentCore identity or policy features. Secure data work requires quality, privacy, integrity, lineage, and controlled access. Application defenses address prompt injection, leakage, toxicity, validation, filtering, logging, and vulnerabilities. RAG grounding, validation, and confidence scoring can reduce hallucination risk.
content.question_focus: Selecting a security control, protecting data, documenting provenance, or improving output grounding.

topics.name: Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
subtopics: AWS Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail, and Trusted Advisor
data lifecycle, logging, residency, monitoring, observation, and retention
policies, review cadence, governance frameworks, transparency, and team training

content.scope_summary: AWS Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail, and Trusted Advisor support governance or compliance activities. Data governance addresses lifecycle, residency, monitoring, observability, logging, and retention. Organizations follow policies, review schedules, review strategies, governance frameworks, transparency standards, and training requirements to maintain governance protocols.
content.question_focus: Choosing a governance service, data-governance control, or organizational review process.
